name: GridShedWatch
description: A benchmark for early warning of US grid supply-shortfall emergencies: 10 documented events (v2.0), frozen hourly EIA-930 data for 48 balancing authorities, and fixed event-level scoring at matched alert budgets.
citeAs: Heiserman, S. (2026). GridShedWatch: a benchmark for early warning of grid load sheds. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23626223
rai:dataCollection: Hourly demand, day-ahead demand forecast and net generation for each balancing authority were pulled from the EIA Open Data API (EIA-930) in October 2026 and frozen with SHA-256 checksums. Events and onset times were compiled by hand from operators' post-event reports and regulatory filings, NERC and FERC-NERC reports, and DOE OE-417 incident reports; every onset cites an official source and an independent second source.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Hours missing any of demand, forecast or net generation, or failing a bad-data filter set from 2019 (values at or below zero, or above twice the 2019 99.9th percentile), are dropped. Five signals are derived by one fixed rule: forecast error, imbalance, and seasonal anomalies of demand, net generation and imbalance. Grids need 90% coverage in 2019 and in 2020-2026; flat-demand and forecast-reporting flags are recorded, not used to drop grids.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The only labels are event onset times. An event qualifies by a rule fixed in advance: Tier 1, an operator-initiated firm load shed of at least 250 MW caused by insufficient supply; Tier 2, an EEA 3 (NERC definition) for lack of supply with a documented emergency action and no firm load shed. Onset is the emergency declaration time; where it is unpublished, a fallback fixed in advance moves onset earlier, never later. Every candidate checked and every exclusion is recorded with its reason (docs/events.md, docs/tier2_candidates.yaml).
rai:annotationsPerItem: One onset per event, set by the author from cited sources; Tier 1 onsets were re-checked against their official documents.
rai:dataLimitations: Ten events, seven from two winter storms (Uri, Elliott); US balancing authorities reporting to EIA-930 only; hourly totals, so events in a small part of a large balancing authority are diluted; no weather or unit-outage data. Events are a complete case series under the rule, not a sample, so detection rates do not estimate operational performance. The replay treats each hourly value as available at its time stamp; live EIA-930 data arrive with a delay.
rai:dataBiases: Heat-driven and other non-winter shortfalls are underrepresented. Three Tier 1 events were used to design the shared alert rules, so results on them are not independent tests. Pretrained models may have seen public EIA-930 data. One reference method (HTM, via htm-monitor) is the author's own; it is scored by the same code as the others.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. All data are aggregate grid totals and public reports.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended: comparing early-warning methods for supply-shortfall grid emergencies on public data at matched alert budgets, including lead time and false-alarm burden on grids without events. Not intended: estimating operational detection rates, detecting transmission or distribution failures, ranking methods on differences of about one event, or replacing operators' situational awareness.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Better early warning of supply shortfalls could give operators and the public more time to prepare for emergencies that have cost lives (at least 210 deaths in Uri). The benchmark is not an operational tool; a method that does well here has been tested on few events and on public data only.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Versioned releases archived on Zenodo; each release freezes its events, data and scoring, and earlier versions stay reproducible from their tags. New qualifying events enter a new version scored with the frozen rules; corrections are made in a new version with the change and its source recorded. Maintained by the author through GitHub issues and pull requests.

distribution.name: events-csv
distribution.description: The scored events of the release (from gridshedwatch/events.yaml and docs/tier2_candidates.yaml).

distribution.name: quality-csv
distribution.description: Every grid of the release with its coverage and data-quality flags.

distribution.name: eia930-files
distribution.description: Frozen hourly EIA-930 data, one gzipped CSV per balancing authority; checksums in each snapshot folder's SHA256SUMS.

recordSet.name: events
recordSet.description: 8 Tier 1 load sheds and 2 Tier 2 EEA 3 emergencies; onset times are the only labels.

field.name: tier
field.description: 1: firm load shed; 2: EEA 3 without firm load shed.

field.name: grid
field.description: Grid id (see the grids record set).

field.name: onset_utc
field.description: Onset, UTC (emergency declaration or fixed fallback).

field.name: onset_basis
field.description: What the onset time is and where it comes from.

recordSet.name: grids
recordSet.description: Grids of the release (one balancing authority each) with coverage and data-quality flags.

field.name: flat_flag
field.description: Demand unchanged for 48 h or more.

field.name: shift_flag
field.description: Forecast error outside its 2019 range in at least 25% of hours.

recordSet.name: eia930
recordSet.description: Hourly EIA-930 totals per balancing authority, Jan 2019 to Oct 2026, UTC.

field.name: eia930_respondent
field.description: Balancing authority code, from the file name.
